sourceChecks.claim: Cloudflare lookup steps 8-10 explicitly separate returned IP from HTTP; cache section permits reuse. This supports name discovery, not path routing or application-health proof.
AWS resolution sequence follows resolver to root, TLD and authority and returns to browser. RFC1034 sections 2.4/5.3.1 also checked for zone and stub roles and cached referrals.
AWS A/AAAA sections identify address families; CNAME section maps to another name. RFC1034 alias processing supports target resolution rather than direct address supply.

RFC8767 explicitly permits expired reuse when refresh fails; RFC1034 TTL discussion supports per-cache age and advance reduction. Timeline and no universal cutover follow from those independent caches.
RFC9520 sections 1-2 distinguish NXDOMAIN/NODATA from resolution failure and require failure caching; negative results use their own SOA-derived TTL, not a later positive record.

AWS explicitly requires configured health checks and answer selection. Shared resolver caching and separate subsequent HTTP connections explain non-proportional request counts and lack of migration; replacement capacity is a necessary operational condition.

RFC1034 sections 2.3-2.4 and 5.3.1 describe redundancy, distributed cache updates, name/type queries and recursive dependence; multiple servers do not repair shared wrong records. HTTP success/error diagnosis follows the separate HTTP stage checked in card 1.

RFC4033 sections 2-4 identify authentication chains, origin/integrity and no confidentiality. TLS identity followup RFC9525 specifies certificate service-identity verification; the requested reference identity must not be replaced by an arbitrary DNS alias.
